arxiv-2004-14337.title: Performance satisfaction in Harpy, a thruster-assisted bipedal robot
arxiv-2004-14337.creator: Pravin Dangol, Alireza Ramezani, Nader Jalili
arxiv-2004-14337.description: Abstract We will report our efforts in designing feedback for the thruster-assisted walking of a bipedal robot. We will assume for well-tuned supervisory controllers and will focus on fine-tuning the desired joint trajectories to satisfy the performance being sought. In doing this, we will devise an intermediary filter based on the emerging idea of reference governors.

arxiv-2007-05637.title: Multilevel Digital Contact Tracing
arxiv-2007-05637.creator: Gautam Mahapatra, Priodyuti Pradhan, Abhinandan Khan, Sanjit Kumar Setua, Rajat Kumar Pal, Ayush Rathor
arxiv-2007-05637.description: Abstract Digital contact tracing plays a crucial role in alleviating an outbreak, and designing multilevel digital contact tracing for a country is an open problem due to the analysis of large volumes of temporal contact data. We develop a multilevel digital contact tracing framework that constructs dynamic contact graphs from the proximity contact data.

arxiv-2012-04360.title: Planning Optical Networks for Unexpected Traffic Growth
arxiv-2012-04360.creator: Sai Kireet Patri (1,2), Achim Autenrieth (1), Jörg-Peter Elbers (1), Carmen Mas Machuca (2)
arxiv-2012-04360.description: Abstract 1 Introduction With 5G deployment becoming a reality across countries, core network operators are realising that deployed optical networks need to be upgraded to quickly capitalize gains. Due to the recent pandemic, many network operators (e.g., BT and Telefónica), have reported a 30-50% increase in broadband traffic in Q1 2020, compared to Q4 2019 [ 1 ] .

arxiv-2205-12884.title: Transfer of energy from flexural to torsional modes for the Fish-bone Suspension bridge
arxiv-2205-12884.creator: Clelia Marchionna, Stefano Panizzi
arxiv-2205-12884.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Clelia Marchionna, Stefano Panizzi. We consider a conservative coupled oscillators systems which arises as a simplified model of the interaction of flexural and torsional modes of vibration along the deck of the so-called fish-bone [ 4 ] model of suspension bridges. The elastic response of the cables is supposed to be asymptotically linear under traction, and asymptotically constant when compressed (a generalization of the slackening regime).

arxiv-2210-04294.title: Skeleton2Humanoid: Animating Simulated Characters for Physically-plausible Motion In-betweening Conference: Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Multimedia; October 10–14, 2022; Lisboa, Portugal Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM ’22), October 1
arxiv-2210-04294.creator: Yunhao Li, Zhenbo Yu, Yucheng Zhu, Bingbing Ni, Guangtao Zhai, Wei Shen
arxiv-2210-04294.description: Abstract . Human motion synthesis is a long-standing problem with various applications in digital twins and the Metaverse. However, modern deep learning based motion synthesis approaches barely consider the physical plausibility of synthesized motions and consequently they usually produce unrealistic human motions.

arxiv-2409-04193.title: Periodic systems have new classes of synchronization stability
arxiv-2409-04193.creator: Sajad Jafari, Atiyeh Bayani, Fatemeh Parastesh, Karthikeyan Rajagopal, Charo I. del Genio, Ludovico Minati, Stefano Boccaletti
arxiv-2409-04193.description: Abstract The Master Stability Function is a robust and useful tool for determining the conditions of synchronization stability in a network of coupled systems. While a comprehensive classification exists in the case in which the nodes are chaotic dynamical systems, its application to periodic systems has been less explored.

arxiv-2410-17407.title: Morita theory for dynamical von Neumann algebras
arxiv-2410-17407.creator: Joeri De Ro
arxiv-2410-17407.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Joeri De Ro. Given a locally compact quantum group G \mathbb{G} and two G \mathbb{G} - W ∗ W^{*} -algebras α : A ↶ G \alpha:A\curvearrowleft\mathbb{G} and β : B ↶ G \beta:B\curvearrowleft\mathbb{G} , we study the notion of equivariant W ∗ W^{*} -Morita equivalence ( A , α ) ∼ G ⁡ ( B , β ) (A,\alpha)\sim{G}(B,\beta) , which is an equivariant version of Rieffel’s notion of W ∗ W^{*} -Morita equivalence.

arxiv-2508-04492.title: Learning Robust Intervention Representations with Delta Embeddings
arxiv-2508-04492.creator: Panagiotis Alimisis, Christos Diou
arxiv-2508-04492.description: Abstract Causal representation learning has attracted significant research interest during the past few years, as a means for improving model generalization and robustness. Causal representations of interventional image pairs, have the property that only variables corresponding to scene elements affected by the intervention / action are changed between the start state and the end state.

arxiv-2510-11589.title: QDER: Query-Specific Document and Entity Representations for Multi-Vector Document Re-Ranking Conference: Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 13–18, 2025; Padua, Italy Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Co
arxiv-2510-11589.creator: Shubham Chatterjee, Jeff Dalton
arxiv-2510-11589.description: Abstract . Neural IR has advanced through two distinct paths: entity-oriented approaches leveraging knowledge graphs and multi-vector models capturing fine-grained semantics. We introduce QDER , a neural re-ranking model that unifies these approaches by integrating knowledge graph semantics into a multi-vector model.

pmc-11358908.title: Mechanomyography-Based Metric Scale for Spasticity: A Pilot Descriptive Observational Study
pmc-11358908.creator: Elgison L dos Santos, Eduardo M Scheeren, Guilherme N Nogueira-Neto, Eddy Krueger, Nathalia Peixoto, Percy Nohama, Christian Peham
pmc-11358908.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). (1) Background: The Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) is commonly used clinically to evaluate spasticity, but its qualitative nature introduces subjectivity. We propose a novel metric scale to quantitatively measure spasticity using mechanomyography (MMG) to mitigate these subjective effects. (2) Methods: The flexor and extensor muscles of knee and elbow joints were assessed with the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) during the acquisition of mechanomyography (MMG) data. The median absolute amplitude of the MMG signals was utilized as a key descriptor.

pmc-11517253.title: Usability of an AI-based independent pedestrian navigation device designed for blind people
pmc-11517253.creator: M Dascal, O Blaga, M Padure, C Amariei
pmc-11517253.description: Background2.2 billion people live with visual impairment (VI) worldwide and face orientation and mobility challenges in various aspects of their lives. Despite technological advancements, the most used mobility solutions for VI are still the walking cane and the guide dog. The objective of this research is to assess the system usability of an AI-based independent pedestrian navigation device (.

pmc-12454083.title: Ureteral reconstruction is safe and successful in poorly functioning kidneys
pmc-12454083.creator: Logan W. Grimaud, Kiran Sury, Matthew Salvino, Austin Livingston, Aaron C. Lentz, Andrew C. Peterson
pmc-12454083.description: ObjectivesPatients with a poorly functioning kidney, defined as less than 20% differential renal function, have historically been considered poor candidates for ipsilateral ureteral reconstruction for stricture. To determine if renal function can be safely preserved in poorly functioning kidneys with ureteral stricture, we evaluated patient outcomes following ureteral reconstruction.

pmc-12528894.title: Biochemical characterization of a flavodiiron protein from bird parasite Histomonas meleagridis: superoxide as a reaction intermediate
pmc-12528894.creator: Subrata Munan, Belem Yoval-Sánchez, Canglin Yao, Javier Seravalli, Evana N Abdulaziz, Mina L Heacock, Achyuta Ramesh, Alexander Galkin, Valentin Cracan
pmc-12528894.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Histomonas meleagridis is a parasitic protozoan which causes histomoniasis (blackhead disease) in a wide range of birds, including domesticated chickens and turkeys, representing a significant health problem in avian veterinary medicine. Despite being classified as an anaerobic parasite, H. meleagridis can survive transient exposure to oxygen (O2) while little is known about the mechanisms that allow this organism to cope with exposure to varying O2 levels.

pmc-12690269.title: Abundant Recurrent Mitochondrial Mutations and Widespread Mitonuclear Epistasis in Caenorhabditis elegans
pmc-12690269.creator: Tuc H M Nguyen, Daniel A Klein, Olivia S Weklar, Erin R Wengrow, Matthew V Rockman
pmc-12690269.description: Coordinated genetic and physical interactions between mitochondrial and nuclear gene products regulate ATP production in the mitochondria. Linking mitochondrial genotypes and mitonuclear genetic interactions to phenotypes remains a complex challenge. Here, we have developed Caenorhabditis elegans as a model for mitonuclear epistasis studies.

pmc-12729987.title: Evaluation of Three Recombinant Antigens for the Detection of Anti-Coxiella Antibodies in Cattle
pmc-12729987.creator: Barbara Colitti, Consiglia Longobardi, Gabriela Flores-Ramirez, Chiara Nogarol, Ludovit Skultety, Gianmarco Ferrara, E Helen Kemp
pmc-12729987.description: Background/Objectives: The detection of anti-Coxiella antibodies using serological methods is essential for identifying exposed ruminants and preventing this important zoonotic disease in livestock. In recent years, numerous attempts have been made to increase diagnostic performance as well as simplify the production of serological assays.

pmc-12892117.title: In Response to “Concerns Regarding Masataka et al.'s ‘Revisiting the Gateway Drug Hypothesis for Cannabis’”
pmc-12892117.creator: Yuji Masataka, Toshihiko Matsumoto
pmc-12892117.description: We clarify Dr. Narita's concerns by replacing subjective wording with data‐based statements, emphasizing the descriptive—not causal—nature of our analysis, and noting that logistic regression was exploratory. Our findings show both progression and non‐progression pathways, indicating no single dominant gateway pattern among Japanese cannabis users. Dear Editor‐in‐Chief, We thank Dr. Narita for the thoughtful comments on our article [1].

pmc-13235481.title: Erythema nodosum as a rare presentation of pulmonary tuberculosis in adolescents: A case report
pmc-13235481.creator: Harold Escudero-Quintero, Diana Marcela Mosquera-Romero, Juliana Taborda-Merchán
pmc-13235481.description: Aim and backgroundTuberculosis (TB), caused by the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, is a multisystemic infectious disease with variable clinical manifestations. Pulmonary involvement is the most common presentation, whereas cutaneous manifestations are rare. Early diagnosis and timely treatment are essential to prevent organ damage, reduce long-term sequelae, and minimize psychosocial impact, particularly in children and adolescents.

pmc-13247963.title: Parameter response mapping does not enhance the correlations of conventional CT quantitative metrics with lung function and subjective symptoms in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
pmc-13247963.creator: Chun Fang, Shuyang Fang, Yin Wang, Jiacheng Guan, Dandan Xiao, Hua Xiao
pmc-13247963.description: BackgroundParameter response mapping (PRM) has been employed in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) assessments, providing a more accurate characterization of emphysema and air trapping. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the correlations of PRM and conventional computed tomography (CT) quantitative metrics with lung function and subjective symptoms in COPD patients.

pmc-13423314.title: Functional dyspepsia redefined: evidence supporting inflammatory dyspepsia – a systematic review
pmc-13423314.creator: Lauren Phang, Alice Kim, Chunlong Mu, Kamran Rostami
pmc-13423314.description: Aim:With growing evidence linking food antigens to inflammation and symptoms, our objective was to review the evidence for the impact of dietary factors on functional dyspepsia (FD) pathogenesis.Background: FD is a common gastrointestinal disorder characterised by postprandial fullness, early satiety, epigastric pain, and burning.

pmc-13424782.title: Exploring the landscape of programmed cell death protein-1 and cluster of differentiation 28 positive T cells and cytokines in non-small cell lung cancer: A retrospective case-control study
pmc-13424782.creator: Ying Yang, Rui-Cheng Li, Changkun Lyu, Weibin Zhang, Yanmin Sun, Ran Xie

pmc-13453515.title: Research note: Zic5 alters digit morphology during avian limb development☆
pmc-13453515.creator: Yining Tang, Shanshan Li, Shibin Bai, Songyang Shang, Ziqiu Jia, Junpeng Zhang, David M. Irwin, Shuyi Zhang, Zhe Wang
pmc-13453515.description: Avian limbs have evolved precise digit lengths and shapes that are optimized for flight and locomotion, but the transcriptional regulators that regulate this architecture remain poorly defined. Although anteriorly biased Zic3 expression constrains digit outgrowth, whether other zinc finger of the cerebellum (Zic) factors—particularly Zic5—shape avian distal limb morphology remains unknown.
